data_sources.name: dunnhumby The Complete Journey (real retail transactions)
data_sources.terms: dunnhumby terms: data may be used solely for research, personal or non-commercial purposes

what_this_is: a household-level offers head consuming pre-cut backbone household embeddings against a real redemption outcome; the honest question is whether embeddings add anything over counts plus demographics
not_causal: campaigns in this corpus were targeted by the retailer, not randomized; nothing here estimates what an offer causes. The causal offers exhibit in this project remains the Criteo randomized-uplift result.

label.definition: household has >=1 coupon_redempt row with DAY >= 599 (the corpus cut)

universe.split: household-disjoint (one row per household; the row split is the household split)
universe.demographics_note: the 2023 re-release anonymized demographic columns to classification_1..5 + HOMEOWNER_DESC + KID_CATEGORY_DESC; households without a demographic row carry 'NA' codes

control_plus_embeddings.features: control features + pre-cut pooled backbone household embedding (512d) + has_history flag

bootstrap.method: household-clustered paired bootstrap (singleton clusters = row bootstrap; shipped machinery)

scale_caveat: ~2,500 households and a rare positive; the positive counts above are the whole story and the intervals are wide
required_sentence: On this corpus the backbone's pre-cut household embeddings add measurable signal over the counts-plus-demographics control for post-cut coupon redemption (AUC delta +0.0269, 95% interval [0.0023, 0.0551] above zero). This is a predictive statement about targeted campaigns, not a causal one.

check.note: rerun with the same --threads as the producing run; deterministic LightGBM settings are on
